nodes.label: Committed graph.json diff churn is expected
nodes.norm_label: committed graph.json diff churn is expected
nodes.rationale: graph.json is rewritten whole on every build, so a large pull request diff is normal. Do not flag it as churn and do not suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks.

nodes.label: Keep graph current: run graphify update . after code changes
nodes.norm_label: keep graph current: run graphify update . after code changes
nodes.rationale: The update is AST-only with no API cost, so it is cheap to run after every code modification.

nodes.label: Graph-first rule: graphify query before grep or source read
nodes.norm_label: graph-first rule: graphify query before grep or source read
nodes.rationale: Queries return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output. Applies when graphify-out/graph.json exists, and the rule must also be put in every subagent prompt that explores code. Raw files are read only for lines the graph or an earlier read already located.

nodes.label: Logo transparent padding (cropped via object-cover)
nodes.rationale: The 2000x1090 canvas is mostly transparent: the artwork occupies only x 84-1858 and y 356-711, about 33% of the canvas height. RootLayout (md:hidden mobile header, h-8), Sidebar (h-12) and the landing Navbar (h-20) place the image in fixed-height boxes with object-cover, which crops the empty vertical margin so the lockup fills the box. SplashScreen (object-contain) and the landing Footer (h-10 w-auto) render the whole canvas, padding included, so the Footer artwork renders small. The cropping intent is inferred from the classes. Replacing the asset with a tightly cropped logo would make object-cover clip the sides of the lockup in those boxes.

The app imports only Logoibpulse.webp (Navbar, Footer, Sidebar, SplashScreen, RootLayout); a repo-wide search found no reference to logo1.png, so it looks like an unused alternate design. 2816x1536 PNG, about 4.2 MB.

nodes.rationale: Mixed-case 'ib' + 'P' + 'ulse' in a bold geometric sans, dark charcoal. Spells the product name shown in the index.html title ('ibPulse - By IBSYSTEMS.SRL') and in logo alt text in Footer, the landing Navbar and SplashScreen.

nodes.rationale: Orange accent with dark charcoal type on white; a recolor of the red and black scheme in Logoibpulse1.webp. Why this palette exists (alternate brand option or abandoned variant) is not documented.

nodes.label: Pulse icon (orange rounded square)
nodes.rationale: Square icon with a white ECG line reads as a live pulse on project health, matching the name ibPulse and the tracker purpose. Inferred from name and motif; no source file states it.

nodes.label: Square i-dot (orange)
nodes.rationale: The round dot of the 'i' is replaced by a rounded square at ascender height, echoing the icon's rounded-square shape to tie wordmark and icon together. The same device appears in Logoibpulse.webp and Logoibpulse1.webp (red), so it looks like a brand-wide invariant.

nodes.label: App-Icon Form Factor (icon-only square master)
nodes.rationale: Square 2048x2048 RGB PNG (about 4.9 MB, no alpha channel), icon-only with no wordmark: one full-bleed rounded tile (corner radius about 18% of width) with opaque white corners and a single centered glyph. The shape suits deriving app icon, favicon and apple-touch-icon sizes. Nothing in src imports logo.png (UI components import the roughly 78 KB Logoibpulse.webp) and root public/ is empty although index.html links favicon and apple-touch-icon files. Intent is inferred, not stated.

nodes.label: Pulse / Heartbeat Metaphor (echoes the ibPulse name)
nodes.norm_label: pulse / heartbeat metaphor (echoes the ibpulse name)
nodes.rationale: A rising and falling heartbeat (ECG) trace reads as 'pulse'. It echoes the product name ibPulse (index.html title 'ibPulse - By IBSYSTEMS.SRL'; sibling logo1.png pairs the same glyph with an 'ibPulse' wordmark) and connotes liveness, health and real-time activity of tracked work. Inferred: the image itself contains no text.

nodes.label: Heartbeat pulse metaphor
nodes.rationale: The name contains 'Pulse' and the symbol is a white ECG heartbeat waveform running edge to edge across a red tile. Together they signal vitality and live health status. For a project tracker (ibPulse by IBSYSTEMS.SRL) this most likely conveys real-time project status and health. This intent is inferred from the artwork and the product context; the image does not state it.

nodes.label: Red rounded-square motif
nodes.rationale: The icon tile and the dot above the 'i' are both solid red rounded squares. Reusing one shape in the symbol and in the wordmark ties the two halves into a single lockup and replaces the round dot of a normal 'i' with a brand-specific accent. The design intent is inferred from the visible repetition.

nodes.label: Logo CSS filter treatments (dark:brightness-200, invert)
nodes.rationale: The logo is a single transparent-background WebP whose wordmark is pure black (rgb 0,0,0 at alpha 255), so it would vanish on dark surfaces. Components adapt this one asset with Tailwind filters instead of loading a per-theme asset: the RootLayout mobile header and the Sidebar header use dark:brightness-200, and SplashScreen stacks an invert copy with an animate-pulse copy. The dark-mode intent is inferred from the dark: prefixes. Caveat: brightness() scales RGB, so it brightens the red and grey emblem but cannot lighten the pure black wordmark. The purpose of the inverted duplicate in SplashScreen is unclear because its container is bg-white and not theme-aware.

nodes.label: Watchful eye metaphor
nodes.rationale: The emblem reads as a stylized eye: two opposed red swooshes form the lids around a transparent gap, and a grey metallic sphere acts as iris and pupil. For a project tracker (ibPulse by IBSYSTEMS.SRL) this most likely conveys watching over project status. This intent is inferred from the artwork and product context; the image does not state it.

nodes.label: Configuración Concierge (founder-led migration and setup)
nodes.rationale: Data migration is the number one barrier to switching software. Migrating data, logos and clients for the customer removes that friction and justifies trying the service. Presented as the founder's competitive advantage.

nodes.norm_label: free or vip access in exchange for feedback and testimonials

nodes.label: Hook: unlimited users for a fixed price
nodes.norm_label: hook: unlimited users for a fixed price
nodes.rationale: Per-user pricing in expensive tools such as Asana and Jira is the pain point. A flat price with unlimited users is the main differentiator.
